definition: Rows    compute_final's own path, by import: R's re-run rows -> apply_rescue -> A36.flagged rows left out. Gate G1 proves they are the same rows. Plans   the recorded plan cell of each row (<ns>/plan.jsonl, latest row of r["cell"]); never regenerated. Gate G4 proves it is the scored plan. Goals   the gold item's goal clauses, as the scorer's goal check reads them. Each clause becomes one plan_walk predicate (CLAUSE below). Walk    plan_walk.World, the executor's action model, unchanged. Its start is the recorded truth of each clause at reset (the capture's state file,         labels.goal_clauses, after the item's setup; extracted into inputs/l3_reset_states.json), so a clause already true and left alone is not "missing". A clause is missing when it is False after the last step. Each L3 failure gets one class: no_plan (plan_status != ok), misses_end_state (at least one clause False on paper), reaches_on_paper (none False). On the same plans, the two preconditions plan_walk.check_plan tests (slice without the ButterKnife in hand, toggle_on Microwave with its door open) are counted per class: such a plan can reach its end-states on paper and still be a planning error. Separately, how it ended (compute_final.failure_breakdown's definition): refused_plan / all_steps_no_goal / failed_skill_step. Counts are plain presentation counts, no weighting and no bootstrap.

gates.gate: G0 gold file is the one the scorer verified
G1 failure_breakdown recomputed from these rows equals final_results.json, all levels and arms
G1b the input re-run rows have the hashes final_results.json recorded
G2 per arm and kitchen: L3 presentations and failure flags reproduce final_results.json rates exactly
G3 all steps ran without the goal equals the recorded diagnostics (K1 G+M 27 of 55, O+M 4 of 55; K2, K3 as recorded)
G4 the recorded plan is the scored plan (status, PC and TDS recomputed, length, executed steps a prefix of the plan)
G5 every gold reference plan reaches its goal on paper; no clause outside the action model
